Review pull request #9161 of Effect-TS/effect: "Fix Duration losing nanosecond precision for large integer millisecond values".

The working directory is a checkout of the repository at the PR's squash-merge commit, so `git diff HEAD~1` is the PR diff (it is also pasted below). Dependencies are installed: `pnpm test --run <test file>` works from the repository root. Every command is limited to 3 minutes, so run targeted test files and small `node` probes; do not run `pnpm check`, `pnpm lint` or the whole suite.

Do the review in this order:
1. Read the changed code and enough of the surrounding implementation to judge it.
2. Run the test file(s) the change touches, and at least one ad-hoc probe of the new behaviour (for example a scratchpad script run with `node`).
3. Report each finding with `reportFinding`, anchored on a line of the diff. Report at least two findings; a question or a nit counts when there is nothing serious. When a call is rejected, read the error and fix the call.
4. Once you have test or probe results, append them to the relevant finding's thread with `updateThread`.
5. Finish with `taskComplete`, giving a short verdict (approve or request changes) and why.

PR description:
Follow-up to #9109. `roundMillisToNanos` still multiplies millis by 1e6 as a double, which stops being exact past about 5.76e11 ms (around 18 years). Epoch timestamps are well past that:

```ts
const ms = 1_760_450_000_123
Duration.toHrTime(Duration.millis(ms))
// [1760450000, 123000064], should be [1760450000, 123000000]
Duration.equals(Duration.millis(ms), Duration.nanos(BigInt(ms) * 1_000_000n))
// false
```

Integer millis now convert with `BigInt(millis) * 1_000_000n`, which is exact and also covers the overflow case from #9109, since any value large enough to overflow is an integer. Fractional millis keep the existing rounding. `Hash` goes through the same helper, so it stays consistent with `equals`.

Added an assert to the existing `toNanosUnsafe` test that fails on main.

Diff:
```diff
diff --git a/.changeset/duration-large-millis-precision.md b/.changeset/duration-large-millis-precision.md
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..0d66a852e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.changeset/duration-large-millis-precision.md
@@ -0,0 +1,5 @@
+---
+"effect": patch
+---
+
+Fix `Duration` conversions losing nanosecond precision for large integer millisecond values.
diff --git a/packages/effect/src/Duration.ts b/packages/effect/src/Duration.ts
index 8d66cfa28..5d4a3a402 100644
--- a/packages/effect/src/Duration.ts
+++ b/packages/effect/src/Duration.ts
@@ -38,10 +38,8 @@ const bigint1e9 = BigInt(1_000_000_000)
 
 const roundTiesAwayFromZero = (input: number): bigint => BigInt(Math.sign(input) * Math.round(Math.abs(input)))
 
-const roundMillisToNanos = (millis: number): bigint => {
-  const nanos = millis * 1_000_000
-  return Number.isFinite(nanos) ? roundTiesAwayFromZero(nanos) : BigInt(millis) * bigint1e6
-}
+const roundMillisToNanos = (millis: number): bigint =>
+  Number.isInteger(millis) ? BigInt(millis) * bigint1e6 : roundTiesAwayFromZero(millis * 1_000_000)
 
 const fromNanosNumber = (nanos: number): Duration => make(Number.isFinite(nanos) ? roundTiesAwayFromZero(nanos) : nanos)
 
diff --git a/packages/effect/test/Duration.test.ts b/packages/effect/test/Duration.test.ts
index 1ba19fa12..f0c969ad0 100644
--- a/packages/effect/test/Duration.test.ts
+++ b/packages/effect/test/Duration.test.ts
@@ -566,6 +566,7 @@ describe("Duration", () => {
     strictEqual(Duration.millis(-0.0000015).pipe(Duration.toNanosUnsafe), -2n)
     strictEqual(Duration.millis(100).pipe(Duration.toNanosUnsafe), 100_000_000n)
     strictEqual(Duration.millis(2 ** 1023).pipe(Duration.toNanosUnsafe), 1_000_000n << 1023n)
+    strictEqual(Duration.millis(1_760_450_000_123).pipe(Duration.toNanosUnsafe), 1_760_450_000_123_000_000n)
   })
```
